items.q: Centor criteria comprise fever, exudate, tender anterior nodes and what fourth feature?
items.exp: Absence of cough favours streptococcal over viral pharyngitis (cough, coryza, hoarseness point viral). Age modifies score in McIsaac version.
r: Incorrect. Cough argues viral.
Correct. No cough is fourth Centor point.
Incorrect. Hoarseness is viral clue.
Incorrect. Conjunctivitis suggests viral or allergic.

items.q: Young adult with trismus, drooling, hot potato voice and uvula pushed to opposite side most likely has what?
items.exp: Quinsy unilateral peritonsillar collection displaces uvula away, locks jaw via pterygoid irritation and muffles voice; drainage plus antibiotics is definitive. Epiglottitis stridors with tripod in children pattern.
r: Incorrect. Bilateral disease lacks deviation and trismus.
Correct. Peritonsillar abscess quinsy.
Incorrect. Epiglottitis airway signs dominate differently.
Incorrect. Dental pain localises jaw teeth without uvula shift.
items.kp: Uvula pushed, jaw locked: drain quinsy.

items.q: Paradise tonsillectomy frequency pattern for recurrent tonsillitis is what?
o: 7 in 1 year, or 5 per year for 2 years, or 3 per year for 3 years documented
Any sore throats counted by memory
items.exp: Documented disabling episodes meeting Paradise thresholds (with features like fever, nodes, exudate, treatment) justify surgery discussion; watchful waiting suits fewer episodes as many remit.
r: Incorrect. Three in one year insufficient alone.
Correct. Seven, five by two, three by three.
Incorrect. Documentation quality matters.
Incorrect. Single quinsy is relative, debated indication.
items.kp: Seven five three unlocks tonsillectomy talk.

items.q: Amoxicillin rash in a fatigued teen with exudative tonsillitis, splenomegaly and atypical lymphocytosis indicates what?
items.exp: Aminopenicillins in acute EBV provoke morbilliform rash (not true allergy in most) with mono syndrome of fatigue, spleen and atypical lymphocytes; spleen rupture precautions and supportive care follow.
r: Incorrect. Rash here is virus drug interaction usually.
Correct. EBV mononucleosis interaction.
Incorrect. Scarlet has sandpaper rash and strawberry tongue strep pattern.
Incorrect. No mucosal blistering syndrome.
items.kp: Mono plus amoxicillin equals rash, not allergy.

items.q: Secondary post tonsillectomy haemorrhage classically occurs when and from what?
o: 5 to 10 days from infection and slough separation
items.exp: Secondary bleeding peaks five to ten days as fibrin slough separates with infection, ranging spit streaks to airway threatening haemorrhage needing urgent ENT return, resuscitation and often theatre arrest.
r: Incorrect. That is primary reactionary bleed under 24h.
Correct. Day five to ten slough infection bleed.
Incorrect. Late bleeds beyond are uncommon.
Incorrect. Discharged patients are peak risk group.
items.kp: Day seven bleed returns to hospital fast.

items.q: Persistent unilateral tonsil enlargement with ulcer and referred ear pain in 60 year old smoker needs what?
o: Urgent suspected cancer pathway: examination, imaging and tonsil histology or biopsy
items.exp: Oropharyngeal squamous carcinoma (and lymphoma) present asymmetrically with otalgia via glossopharyngeal referral and neck nodes; adults need two week wait style urgent assessment, never antibiotic loops.
r: Incorrect. Antibiotics delay cancer diagnosis.
Correct. Urgent cancer pathway with histology.
Incorrect. Adult asymmetry is red flag.
Incorrect. Gargles mask malignancy.
items.kp: One angry tonsil in older adult: cancer pathway.

items.q: HPV positive oropharyngeal cancer increasingly presents in younger non smokers typically with what first sign?
o: Cystic level II neck mass with small occult primary
items.exp: HPV driven tumours hide small tonsil or tongue base primaries while metastasising early to cystic level II nodes, with better treatment response than tobacco cancers; p16 testing guides pathway.
r: Incorrect. Primary often tiny and hidden.
Correct. Cystic neck node, occult primary.
Incorrect. Hoarseness is laryngeal site.
Incorrect. Neck mass often precedes swallowing issues.
items.kp: Young neck cyst may be HPV cancer calling.

items.q: Adenoidectomy in children principally treats which problems?
o: Nasal obstruction, sleep apnoea, selected glue ear and chronic adenoiditis sinusitis
items.exp: Adenoids obstruct posterior nose and Eustachian region, so surgery targets obstructive sleep, mouth breathing and selected otitis or sinus pathways, often combined with tonsillectomy for sleep apnoea.
r: Incorrect. Tonsillectomy addresses tonsillitis.
Correct. Obstruction, sleep and ear indications.
Incorrect. Bleeding treated at vessel source.
Incorrect. Stridor is laryngeal evaluation.
items.kp: Adenoids out for blockage, not sore throats.

items.q: Peritonsillar abscess drainage immediate priority before procedure is what?
o: Airway assessment and readiness, since trismus and swelling can obstruct
items.exp: Most quinsy drain awake with topical anaesthesia safely after airway evaluation, suction and positioning; CT reserves for deep neck suspicion, children, immunocompromise or failed aspiration. Airway deterioration changes to theatre plan.
r: Incorrect. Typical adult quinsy needs no CT.
Correct. Airway readiness first.
Incorrect. Booking follows acute resolution debate.
Incorrect. Undrained pus needs procedure.

items.q: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis treatment chiefly prevents which immune complication in at risk populations?
o: Acute rheumatic fever (antibiotics proven); glomerulonephritis prevention unproven
items.exp: Timely penicillin prevents rheumatic fever and suppurative spread; evidence does not show glomerulonephritis prevention. This drives treatment in high incidence populations more than symptom shortening.
r: Incorrect. PSGN not proven preventable by antibiotics.
Correct. Rheumatic fever prevention is proven goal.
Incorrect. Rash is toxin manifestation, not prevented target.
Incorrect. Quinsy can still occur despite treatment occasionally.
